sections.name: summary
sections.value: Wire the tree-sitter TypeScript and TSX grammars into fs3-parsers so .ts/.tsx files stop being bare file elements (backlog row 147: every TypeScript file in the index today is one unparsed blob — the pij extensions, this repo's own tooling, and most of the fleet's code). The extraction walk is generic; the packet is the two Language entries, the grammar crate, the classify decisions for TypeScript node kinds, a generic value-shape rule so arrow-function bindings (the dominant TS style) become Function elements, fixtures with golden element forests, and a real-usage receipt on prod after re-ingest.

sections.name: goals
value: `.ts`/`.mts`/`.cts` → Language::TypeScript, `.tsx` → Language::Tsx; file subkind reports the language
functions, classes (incl. abstract), interfaces, enums, type aliases, methods, method/function signatures and namespaces become named elements with correct addresses and spans

arrow-function / function-expression bindings (`const f = () => {}`, `export const h = async () => {}`, class-field arrows) become Function elements named by their binding, via a language-agnostic value-shape rule in the generic walk
golden fixture tests for every decision, including the deliberate non-elements, with mutation receipts
prod receipt: after re-ingest of a TS-heavy repo, `flowspace3 search` returns TS function/container elements, not bare files

sections.name: non_goals
value: JavaScript/JSX (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`) — separate packet; tree-sitter-javascript is a different crate
changing ElementKind, the store schema, embeddings, or any CLI envelope
decorators, overload merging, declaration-merging semantics beyond what the generic walk yields
re-ingesting prod yourself — o-prime does the prod re-ingest and takes the receipt

value.claim: `.ts`/`.tsx` fixtures scan into element trees whose language is typescript/tsx and whose forest matches a checked-in golden: function/class/abstract class/interface/enum/type alias/method/method signature/function signature/namespace elements with correct addresses and 1-based spans; a JSX-heavy .tsx file parses without ScanError::Unparseable

arrow-function and function-expression bindings (six shapes in the fixture: const/let/export const/async/generator/class-field arrow) are Function elements named by the binding, produced by a generic value-shape rule in source.rs (no `Language::` branch); removing the rule turns the fixture test red

`internal_module` (namespace) is a Container that scopes the addresses of its members; the classify tests enumerate every TypeScript node-kind decision including the deliberate non-elements (`export_statement`, `lexical_declaration`, `import_statement`)
no regression: rust/python/markdown classify + fixture tests green, `cargo clippy -D warnings` clean, CI gate green on the exact PR sha (or the local exclusive gate)

real usage: a scan of ~/pi-hacking/pij/.pi/extensions/pij/**/*.ts through fs3-parsers reports N>1 elements per file for every file that declares anything (before: exactly 1); after o-prime's prod re-ingest, `flowspace3 search` for a named pij extension function returns a function element from a .ts path

value.title: Phase 1: TypeScript + TSX grammars
value.brief: One coder. Wire the grammar crate and Language entries first (prove the build resolves against tree-sitter 0.26 before anything else), then fixtures + goldens, then the generic value-shape rule and the namespace decision with mutation receipts, then regression + gate, then the pre-prod scan receipt in the PR body.
